## Verdict: FAIL — checklist lines 2 and 3 fail; every other line passes

The hydrology passes every test, including the exit bar's D8 share: 100 % at every rung, on both reliefs and both cell
sizes (CONFIRMED). The river does not hold up. Five design clauses or recorded rules can be broken without any test
failing (five targeted mutants survive), and the report states a wrong `reachesCore`. On the relief fixtures, the exit
bar's river clauses are met only by degraded stubs that lie in the margin and end in a sink. The test skips its outfall
check without saying so.

| failing line | evidence (CONFIRMED unless marked) | required change |
|---|---|---|
| **2 (a)** §4.2 S1 (3) "the inlet lies on the arena's upstream edge (… the requested bearing or **the highest edge**)" has no test that can fail | Mutant K18 takes the **lowest** edge in `inletOf` (`strategy.ts` 201, `m > bestMean` → `m < bestMean`). It **survived**: 41/41 green. `relief-bar.test.ts` runs `river: {}` but never asserts which edge the inlet is on. | Add a test with no bearing where the edges' mean heights differ. Assert that the inlet lies on the highest edge, and that C-0173 (2)'s tie order E, N, W, S holds. K18 must go red. |
| **2 (b)** §4.2 S1 (3) "knots sit **mostly on alternating sides**" (the meander term; the item's `builds`) has no test | Mutant K02 always keeps the previous side (`trace.ts` 109, `u1 < MEANDER_SAME_SIDE ? prev : -prev` → `prev`). It **survived**: 41/41. The knot tests check only offset size, ordinals and endpoints. | Add a test of the side rule over many traces: the share of side changes is near 1 − `MEANDER_SAME_SIDE`, or the sides equal C-0173 (4)'s rule on the draws. K02 must go red. |
| **2 (c)** listed test "F-RIVER's rungs … **move the inlet** — each reached and reported": the rung's effect is unpinned | Mutant K01 never applies the attempt's shift (`strategy.ts` 232). It **survived**: 41/41. `river.test.ts`'s inlet-rung test (≈ line 243, titled "… moves the inlet along its edge") checks only the `ladderUses` rows. The strategy writes those rows whether or not the inlet moved. | Assert that the attempts' inlets differ: attempt a ≥ 1 is shifted along its edge by (u − ½) × the frame's half side and clamped (C-0173 (2)). K01 must go red. |
| **2 (d)** listed rung "**re-trace from the last good knot**" (§5.2 F-RIVER; C-0173 (5)): the re-trace's root is unpinned for a carve or stuck failure | Mutant K03 re-traces every carve or stuck failure from the inlet (`trace.ts` 420, `good = 0`). It **survived**: 41/41. The crater test (`river.test.ts` 114) checks only that a `retrace` event with cause `carve` exists. The self-touch test pins `value === 0`, which is the inlet case. | Add a fixture whose carve failure lies past the second knot. Assert that the event's `value` is the knot before the last knot ahead of the failure (> 0), and that the knots kept before it are unchanged. K03 must go red. |
| **2 (e)** C-0173 (6)'s recorded rule "delivered `full` (tier 0, **2 after a carve or re-trace**, 3 after the inlet rung)" has no test that can fail | Mutant K17 makes `tierOf` return 0 (`strategy.ts` 543). It **survived**: 41/41. The sink test (`river.test.ts` 101) does not read the `requested` row. This is the same pattern as C-0167's precedent: a recorded rule that no test could fail. | Assert the sink fixture's `requested` row: `full` at tier 2. K17 must go red. |
| **2 (f)** `RiverOutcome.reachesCore` ("The course reaches the core before it leaves the frame", `types.ts` 84) is wrong for a degraded river, and no test checks it against the delivered course | The probe ran the exact runs of `relief-bar.test.ts`: CITY, the 3 000 m fixture, `siteContext(3000)`. Output: `"reachesCore":true … course 54 pts … delivered min distance to centre 396635 cm`. With the switch: `course 14 pts … 395829 cm`. The core radius is 125 000 cm (frame 500 000 cm, `CORE_SHARE` 0.25). `strategy.ts` 407 – 408 compute `core` on the untruncated `trace.course`, but 421 delivers the truncated course. | Compute `reachesCore` (and the degraded pick's `dist2`, if it is meant to describe the delivery) on the delivered course. Add a test on a degraded course. |
| **3** no undeclared shortcut: **the exit bar's river clauses on the relief fixtures are silently narrowed** | `relief-bar.test.ts` 98 – 121 ("CITY: a river from the highest edge on both reliefs — D8 100 %, bed monotone, carve ≤ carveMaxCm", with and without `hydroCoarsen`). In all four of its runs the river is degraded: `fits:false`, `outfall:"sink"`, `corridor:false`, `requested` `degraded` tier 4 cause F-RIVER. The delivered courses are stubs of 14 – 54 points lying **entirely in the margin**: nearest approach 3.96 – 4.29 km from the centre, frame half-side 2.5 km. Line 115's `if (out.corridor)` never runs. The remaining asserts hold by construction on a truncated course: `truncated()` cuts until `planCarve` fits, and the carve writes a running minimum. So the bed is "monotone to its outfall" only where the outfall is the sink the stub was cut at. The rate (probe `tally.mts`, 10 terrains per relief class, highest edge and a bearing): at **CITY 0 of 80 rivers are `full`**, and **60 of 60** on rolling, hilly and the 3 000 m acropolis are `nofit` / `sink` (most under 2 km). At TOWN 5 of 80 are `full`, all on plain relief. Diagnosis (`diag.mts`), CONFIRMED: on rolling relief every re-trace failed on `touch`. The bare D8 line from the highest-edge inlet leaves the grid after 3 – 4 cells, so the descent crawls along its own closed edge and folds. Each whole re-trace from the inlet re-runs the same line with only the offsets halved. On the acropolis, carves of 2 038 – 3 902 cm are needed (34 of 313 depressions are deeper than the cap). C-0173 (6) declares the degraded *form*. Nothing declares that the exit-bar fixtures deliver only degraded stubs, and the test reports a pass on them. | The relief-bar test must assert the delivered outcome without conditions (no silent `if (out.corridor)`). The bed-to-outfall and carve bars must be judged on a river that reaches an outfall on the relief fixtures. Do either (i) or (ii). (i) Fix the trace so that rivers on the M0 relief fixtures fit and leave by the frame edge: the inlet's descent must not run back along its own closed edge, and a fold in the descent line itself must not be re-traced only by halving offsets. Then assert `fits`, `outfall:'frame'` and `corridor` on those runs. (ii) If a degraded river is the honest M0 result on these fixtures, assert that outcome per fixture and record it with its measured rate in a choices row. Route it to M0-e-06, whose site-spike bars need a river crossing the town on these same fixtures (the trace crossing the river at water gates; spans through crossing sites). Then judge the bed and outfall clauses on a relief run whose river does reach the frame. |

The fix round re-runs lines 2 and 3 and the item's whole test set. Mutants K01, K02, K03, K17 and K18 must be red, and
the reachesCore probe above must give `false` for the delivered stubs.

  `+ 1` slack. A test without the slack would pin the clamp. Optional.
